items.stimulus: A musicologist timing performances of a traditional work song models the recordings with line $t$ in the xy-plane, where $x$ is the number of verses sung and $y$ is the running time, in minutes. Line $t$ has a y-intercept of $(0, 4)$ and passes through the point $(2, 10)$.
items.stem: The point $(5, b)$ lies on line $t$. What is the value of $b$?
items.explanation: From $(0, 4)$ to $(2, 10)$, y rises 6 while x rises 2, so the slope is $3$. The y-intercept is 4, so line $t$ is $y = 3x + 4$. Substitute $x = 5$: $y = 3(5) + 4 = 19$, so $b = 19$.

B.why: You multiplied the slope by 5 but dropped the y-intercept. $3(5) = 15$ is only part of $3(5) + 4$.

D.why: You used 10, the y-coordinate of the second point, as the y-intercept and wrote $y = 3x + 10$. The y-intercept is 4, from the point $(0, 4)$.
